theme: Winter logging-camp drying wool becomes living cloth: a compact diagonal mitten unfolds into a long hollow sleeve, then unfurls as a broad three-panel quilt riding the wind. Asymmetry, rolled cuffs and off-center seam faces define the actual anatomy; no animal or concealed person.

evolution_design.regional_evidence: Minnesota DNR describes wool clothing, including hand coverings, and difficulty drying wet wool overnight in logging camps. MNHS describes garments suspended overhead in bunkhouses.
evolution_design.original_invention: A self-sewing ghost turns leftover wool into a wind-catching body. The supernatural being, flight, names and behavior are original fiction; no real haunting, human victim or sacred being is represented.

body_growth.body: One compact bent mitten body, conspicuous thumb hook and rolled open cuff. Two staggered rectangular eye windows are embedded along its side seam.
body_growth.silhouette: Diagonal hooked mitten, no separate head or feet.

body_growth.body: Long open sleeve/cuff tube slants down-left from a rolled upper opening. One short loop and one longer low trailing flap break symmetry; its face lies low along the side seam.
body_growth.silhouette: Tall asymmetric folded tube with hanging fringe, no central head or paired raised arms.

body_growth.body: Three sewn quilt panels form a broad diagonally billowing sail. Upper corner unfurls high; opposite corner rolls under; three square fringe tabs trail below. Face remains off-center on far-left seam.
body_growth.silhouette: Wide rising-diagonal patchwork body with rolled corners; no animal head, wings, claws or feet.

habitat: Windy clearings and old winter logging-camp margins in the North Shore forest; encounter placement remains a proposal.

proposed_routes.placement: Proposed optional forest-camp clearing branch near the coastal route, subject to separate map authoring.
proposed_routes.status: encounter concept only; no existing map or script is changed

sources.title: Minnesota DNR — Logging Camps: The Early Years
sources.supports: Wool work clothing and hand coverings; wet wool could fail to dry in the bunkhouse overnight.
sources.fantasy_extension: The wool becomes a living mitten, sleeve and quilt-bodied ghost.

sources.title: Minnesota Historical Society — Logging Industry
sources.supports: Logging-camp garments were suspended overhead to dry in bunkhouses.
sources.fantasy_extension: Suspended fabric becomes sleeve-lift flight and a wind-catching patchwork body.

nonduplication: Dense solid sewn wool with asymmetrical cuffs and quilt panels; unlike Nodcloak prairie-smoke plume. No central round hood, facial disk, beak, symmetrical feather wings, feet, animal under clothing or person wearing a cape.
sprite_constraints: Native 56×56 front full body facing left; 48×48 close rear portrait facing upper-right. Exactly four flat inks per species, independent stage palettes; large exposed eye windows and black pupils; stepped solid black contours. Current native source_center sampling; no painted facial pixels after conversion.
silhouette_concept: Compact diagonal mitten -> long open sleeve tube -> broad diagonal three-panel quilt.
design_lock: Root approved all six asymmetric mitten/sleeve/diagonal-quilt native views; stable F076 and MN163–165 IDs retained.
